description: CompSim computes section properties for slender structures with complex geometry and mixed materials. Its contributors publish MATLAB functions for defining input geometry, calculating mass and stiffness, plotting sections and writing outputs. The own README describes a weighted-average method coupled to Euler–Bernoulli beam theory. A user supplies each candidate cross section and material distribution; the spatial scale is that section, with no built-in region or operating period. The results can support preliminary trade-off studies for wind-turbine blades and other structural components. Current source is public and free under GPL-3.0 in the upstream repository. MATLAB is a separate dependency and may require a paid site licence. A limitation is that a beam-section approximation does not model every three-dimensional stress concentration or failure mode. No related catalogue record was identified. No geometry file, MATLAB function or turbine design was run.
